title: How to create dynamic tables
text: Standard Markdown tables, as shown in the Quarto Markdown Guide, work well for small static datasets. For larger scientific tables requiring live search, sorting, unit conversions, LaTeX math, or literature references, this template provides a custom dynamic-tables filter that renders interactive Tabulator tables directly from .csv files.

title: How to create dynamic tables
text:
Global Options
Global options are specified as key: value pairs at the top of the block:

src: Path to the input .csv file (required).
searchable: Shows or hides the full-row search bar above the table (true or false, default false).
sortable: Enables or disables sorting across all columns (true or false, default true).
per-page: Sets the initial number of rows per page (default 15, with a selector for 10, 15, 25, and 50 rows). The pagination footer hides automatically whenever the active row count fits within one page.

title: How to create dynamic tables
text:
Column Options
Individual columns are configured with col N:, using a 0-based index (col 0: is the first column, col 1: is the second, and so on). Multiple properties for the same column are separated by commas:

header=...: Replaces the CSV header title. Enclose the title in quotes ("..." or '...') if it contains commas; inline math expressions (such as header=$m$) are also supported when latex or latexnum is active (see below).
number / string: Enforces numeric or alphabetical sorting instead of auto-detection (empty cells always sort to the bottom). Numeric columns automatically format extreme magnitudes (\(\vert{}x\vert{} < 10^{-3}\) or \(\vert{}x\vert{} \ge 10^4\)) in exponential notation.
sortable / unsortable: Overrides the global sortable setting for that column.
latex: Renders any LaTeX math syntax ($ ... $, $$ ... $$, \( ... \), or \[ ... \]) in both the column header and cell text via MathJax or KaTeX.
dropdown: Adds a filter menu in the column header populated with all unique values in that column.

::: {.dynamic-table}
src: data/example-table.csv
searchable: true
per-page: 4
col 0: header="Sector", dropdown
col 1: header="Particle", latex
col 2: header="Mass [GeV]", number
col 3: header="Discovery", unsortable
:::

title: How to create dynamic tables
section: Scientific Units, LaTeX Math Numbers, and INSPIRE-HEP Citations
text:
Scientific Units, LaTeX Math Numbers, and INSPIRE-HEP Citations
Three specialized column tags support physical unit scaling, LaTeX scientific notation, and automated bibliography management:

units(Unit1: factor1, Unit2: factor2, ...): Implies number and adds a unit selector to the column header. The first unit listed is active by default; selecting another unit multiplies every numeric cell in the column by its conversion factor.
latexnum: Implies both number and latex, and transforms numeric cells into inline math expressions (1.057e-1 displayed as \(1.06 \times 10^{-1}\)) that update automatically whenever the user switches units.
inspire: Implies string and treats cell values as INSPIRE-HEP TeX citation keys (multiple keys in one cell can be separated by commas or semicolons, with or without a leading @). During compilation, the filter fetches the corresponding BibTeX records from INSPIRE-HEP in batches, turns each valid key into a clickable [N] CitationKey link that highlights the target entry on click, and renders a live reference list directly below the table that updates as rows are searched, filtered, or paginated.

::: {.dynamic-table}
src: data/example-table.csv
searchable: true
per-page: 4
col 0: header="Sector", dropdown
col 1: header="Particle", latex
col 2: header=$m$, latexnum, units(GeV: 1, MeV: 1e3, TeV: 1e-3)
col 3: header="Discovery", inspire, unsortable
:::

title: How to create dynamic plots
text:
Static figures, as shown in the Quarto Markdown Guide, work well for fixed illustrations. For interactive scientific figures requiring zoomable 2D/3D canvases, analytical curve evaluation, tabular data overlays, LaTeX math labels, or animated parameter sweeps, this template provides a custom dynamic-plots filter powered by Plotly.

Decoupled Definitions and Canvas Blocks
A dynamic plot is split into curve definition blocks (which register data or mathematical expressions without rendering anything on their own) and a canvas block (::: {.dynamic-plot}) that combines one or more curve IDs onto a single figure:

::: {.plot-function id="..."}: Defines an analytical 2D or 3D curve or implicit contour/surface.
::: {.plot-file id="..."}: Defines a 2D/3D trace or a slider-driven parameter sweep from a numeric data file.
::: {.dynamic-plot}: Mounts the interactive Plotly canvas, axis styling, collapsible legend sidebar, and sweep controls.

Every .plot-function and .plot-file block requires a unique id attribute so it can be referenced inside curves: (and reused across multiple figures if needed).


Canvas Configuration (dynamic-plot)
The ::: {.dynamic-plot} block accepts key: value options controlling layout, axes, and interactive controls:

curves: Comma-separated list of .plot-function and/or .plot-file IDs to plot together (required). All curves in a plot must share the same dimensionality (all 2D or all 3D), and at most one parameter-sweep curve may be included per plot.
xlabel, ylabel, zlabel: Axis titles. Inline LaTeX math ($ ... $, \( ... \)) is rendered via MathJax or KaTeX.
xscale, yscale, zscale: Axis scaling (linear or log, default linear).
xrange, yrange, zrange: Explicit axis bounds formatted as [min, max]. Bounds must be strictly positive when the corresponding axis uses log scale.
height: Canvas height in pixels (integer \(\ge 200\), default 480).
legend: Shows or hides the collapsible right-hand legend sidebar with per-curve visibility checkboxes (true or false, default true).
play: Displays a compact Play/Pause animation button next to the parameter slider (true or false, default false). Only valid when curves includes a parameter-sweep curve.



Analytical Functions (plot-function)
Use ::: {.plot-function id="..."} to plot explicit functions or implicit equations without pre-generating data files:

expr: Mathematical expression (required). Supported forms:

2D explicit (y = f(x)): Expression in x without = (e.g., sin(x) / x).
2D implicit (f(x, y) = g(x, y)): Equation in x and y containing = (e.g., x^2 + y^2 = 1).
3D explicit (z = f(x, y)): Expression in x and y without = (e.g., x^2 - y^2).
3D implicit (f(x, y, z) = g(x, y, z)): Equation in x, y, and z containing = (e.g., x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1).

label: Legend title, supporting inline LaTeX math (default: the block’s id).
color: Trace or surface CSS color, such as #1f77b4, crimson, or rgb(31, 119, 180) (default: automatic colorway).
xrange, yrange, zrange: Sampling domain [min, max] along each axis (default: the canvas range, co-plotted file extent, or [-10, 10]).
points: Sample resolution per axis, integer \(\ge 2\) (defaults: 100 for 2D explicit, 60 for 2D implicit and 3D explicit, 25 per axis for 3D implicit).
mode: Drawing style for explicit 2D curves (lines, markers, or lines+markers, default lines).
smooth: Enables spline interpolation between sample points (true or false, default true).

Expressions support +, -, *, /, ^, implicit multiplication (2x, x sin(x)), constants (pi, e), and standard functions (sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, sinh, cosh, tanh, exp, log, ln, log10, log2, sqrt, abs, sign, floor, ceil, min, max). Explicit 2D functions automatically resample when zooming or panning.
::: {.plot-function id="wave-sin"}
expr: sin(2 * x) * exp(-0.2 * x)
label: $e^{-0.2x}\sin(2x)$
xrange: [0, 8]
color: #1f77b4
:::

::: {.plot-function id="circle-eq"}
expr: (x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 0.64
label: $(x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 0.8^2$
xrange: [0, 8]
yrange: [-1.2, 1.2]
color: crimson
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: wave-sin, circle-eq
xlabel: $x$
ylabel: $y(x)$
yrange: [-1.2, 1.2]
height: 400
:::



File-Backed Curves and Logarithmic Axes (plot-file)
Use ::: {.plot-file id="..."} to plot numeric columns from .csv, .tsv, or whitespace-delimited text files (blank lines and lines starting with #, %, or // are skipped automatically):

src: Path to the data file (required).
x: Column expression for the horizontal axis using 0-based column tokens (c0, c1, c2, …) and any supported math operators or functions (required).
y: Column expression for the vertical axis (required).
z: Column expression for the third axis in 3D scatter/line plots.
skip: Number of leading non-comment header rows to ignore, integer \(\ge 0\) (default 0).
label: Legend title, supporting inline LaTeX math (default: the block’s id).
color: Trace CSS color (default: automatic colorway).
mode: Drawing style (lines, markers, or lines+markers, default lines+markers).
smooth: Enables spline interpolation (true or false, default false).

::: {.plot-file id="damped-data"}
src: data/example-plot-damped.csv
skip: 1
x: c0
y: c1
label: Measured amplitude
mode: markers
color: #ff7f0e
:::

::: {.plot-function id="damped-model"}
expr: exp(-0.35 * x) * cos(2 * x)
label: $e^{-0.35t}\cos(2t)$
color: #1f77b4
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: damped-data, damped-model
xlabel: Time $t$ [s]
ylabel: Amplitude $A(t)$ [m]
height: 400
:::

Setting yscale: log (or xscale: log) switches the corresponding axis to base-10 logarithmic scaling and automatically filters out non-positive values when computing default axis bounds:
::: {.plot-file id="energy-data"}
src: data/example-plot-damped.csv
skip: 1
x: c0
y: c2
label: Measured energy
mode: markers
color: #2ca02c
:::

::: {.plot-function id="energy-fit"}
expr: exp(-0.70 * x)
label: $E_0 e^{-0.70t}$
color: #1f77b4
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: energy-data, energy-fit
xlabel: Time $t$ [s]
ylabel: Energy $E(t)$ [J]
yscale: log
height: 380
:::



Parameter Sweeps and Animation
When a data file stores multiple snapshots across columns, .plot-file can turn them into an interactive slider sweep:

y: Sweep column range (c1..c7) or explicit comma-separated column list (c1, c3, c5, c7).
param: Numeric parameter values mapped to the selected columns, written either as a uniform range (0..3) or an explicit list (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0) matching the column count (required to enable sweep mode).
param-label: Label shown beside the live parameter readout, supporting inline LaTeX math (default Parameter).
transform: Optional expression applied to every sweep value y and any column tokens cN (e.g., y^2 to plot squared amplitude).

Adding play: true to the enclosing ::: {.dynamic-plot} block places a Play/Pause toggle button directly before the parameter readout:
::: {.plot-file id="wave-sweep"}
src: data/example-plot-sweep.csv
x: c0
y: c1..c7
param: 0..3
param-label: $t$ [s]
label: Wave amplitude
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: wave-sweep
xlabel: $x$ [m]
ylabel: $\psi(x, t)$
play: true
height: 440
:::

You can also derive transformed quantities on the fly with transform: and disable the sidebar with legend: false when plotting a single curve:
::: {.plot-file id="wave-intensity"}
src: data/example-plot-sweep.csv
x: c0
y: c1..c7
param: 0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0
param-label: $t$ [s]
transform: y^2
label: $\vert{}\psi(x, t)\vert{}^2$
color: #9467bd
smooth: true
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: wave-intensity
xlabel: $x$ [m]
ylabel: $\vert{}\psi(x, t)\vert{}^2$
legend: false
height: 400
:::



3D Surfaces, Implicit Volumes, and Trajectories
Combining 3D .plot-function definitions (explicit surfaces or implicit = isosurfaces) with 3D .plot-file definitions (z: specified) renders an interactive WebGL 3D scene supporting orbit rotation, pan, zoom, and per-trace legend toggles:
::: {.plot-function id="saddle-surface"}
expr: 0.25 * (x^2 - y^2)
label: $z = \frac{1}{4}(x^2 - y^2)$
xrange: [-1.5, 1.5]
yrange: [-1.5, 1.5]
points: 40
:::

::: {.plot-function id="unit-sphere"}
expr: x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1
label: $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1$
xrange: [-1.2, 1.2]
yrange: [-1.2, 1.2]
zrange: [-1.2, 1.2]
points: 22
color: #2ca02c
:::

::: {.plot-file id="helix-path"}
src: data/example-plot-3d.csv
x: c0
y: c1
z: c2
label: Helix trajectory
mode: lines+markers
color: #ff7f0e
:::

::: {.dynamic-plot}
curves: saddle-surface, unit-sphere, helix-path
xlabel: x
ylabel: y
zlabel: z
height: 520
:::
